subject: Geo operational runbook for EU pin + transient telemetry transit
messages:
From: Sara Tan <sara.tan@hearthhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@hearthhealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo constraints: EU pin + telemetry transit question

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HearthHealth is excited about Redwood's throughput and the control-plane observability. Before we move to procurement, our security team has two specific asks around data residency:

1) EU pin: all inference requests and embeddings for EU customers must be stored and processed in the EU region.
2) Transient telemetry: we understand some telemetry and operational metrics are routed to the control plane for analysis. Can you explain the maximum transient transit window, where that telemetry is parsed/retained, and provide an operational runbook that outlines failover behavior when an EU region becomes unavailable?

We're particularly interested in:
- whether short-lived telemetry (logs, traces, anonymized perf metrics) ever persist outside EU beyond a short buffer, and for how long;
- what fallbacks you provide (model variant in another region, queued processing) and any customer-configurable pinning policies;
- evidence we can attach to our DPA questionnaire (runbook, matrix of subprocessors, and retention timing).

Could you send us a runbook draft and the subprocessor roster so we can scope the DPA addendum? We're targeting signing by the end of June, so a quick turnaround would be helpful.

Best,
Sara Tan
Head of InfoSec
HearthHealth

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geo constraints: EU pin + telemetry transit question

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Olga (Infra) to pull the runbook + subprocessor ledger together.

Quick summary of our stance so you have an immediate answer:
- EU pinning: customer data and inference execution occur in the EU region for pinned workloads. Model artifacts and derived embeddings remain in-region unless the customer elects snapshot export.
- Telemetry transit: ephemeral operational telemetry (sampling of traces, perf counters) may be streamed to our control plane; default transient window is 6 hours in-flight. We provide a configuration knob to limit retention to 30 minutes for EU-pinned customers.
- Failover: we support a configurable failover window (default 15 minutes queue with canary routing). If a customer requires a strict no-cross-border fallback, we can enable a hold-and-retry queue that suspends requests until EU capacity returns (impacts latency).

I'm attaching an initial runbook outline and a compact residency matrix so you can see the pieces. Olga — can you add the subprocessor snapshot and ETA for the full ledger? Marissa — please flag any DPA language gaps.

Next steps: I'll circulate a polished runbook tomorrow and propose a 30-minute alignment call with HearthHealth security.

Thanks,

Thanks for the draft, Marcus. A few legal/contract points to include in the runbook and DPA addendum: 

- We should offer two explicit telemetry retention profiles for EU-pinned customers: "standard_ephemeral" (30 minutes max) and "strict_ephemeral" (no telemetry leaves region; only aggregate counters in-region). Add config flags and API fields.
- For transient failover, add an optional SLA carve-out: if customer opts into cross-region fallback, include a maximum cross-border window (we suggest 48 hours) and an explicit consent checkbox in the admin console + signature in the DPA addendum.
- Subprocessor roster: provide snapshot with ISO27001 / SOC2 status for each entry and an activation timestamp for any new subprocessor.

Also, add a short section on how to produce evidence: where to pull ephemeral trace retention logs (timebound), how to generate an audit package for tribunal/third-party review, and a contact for emergency escrow of keys (if required).

Olga — can you confirm whether the 6-hour default is still accurate and whether we can expose the 30-minute config at the tenancy level? If yes, Marcus we can push the final runbook and legal text by EOD Friday.

- Marissa
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Geo operational runbook for EU pin + transient telemetry transit

Sara — attaching the consolidated runbook and the residency matrix you asked for. Highlights and decisions we captured: 

- Telemetry retention: default 6-hour buffer for internal routing; we will enable a tenant-level toggle with two profiles (standard_ephemeral = 30 minutes; strict_ephemeral = 0 minutes external transit).
- Failover modes: (1) queue-and-retry (hold up to customer-configured window), (2) redirected to a compatible EU model variant in a different EU zone, (3) opt-in cross-region fallback (requires DPA checkbox + explicit consent, max proposed window 48 hours).
- Subprocessor roster: attached snapshot contains subprocessors + compliance attestations. We will provide per-subprocessor activation timestamps on request.
